# Environmental Gram-negatives: pseudomonads, vibrios and Burkholderia

> *What happens when bacteria adapted to water and soil meet a human host?*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
The layout will match that of [*Gram-positive cocci*](gram-positive-cocci.qmd). The plan:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| The group in one sentence | Gram-negative rods that live in water, soil and the sea, hardy and naturally resistant to many chemicals |
| Sorting key | Must respire or can ferment; salt tolerance; where in the environment they live |
| Main organisms | *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* (water, natural resistance), *Burkholderia pseudomallei* (soil, diabetes as host factor, Singapore relevance), *Vibrio cholerae* (a single toxin) |
| Supporting organisms | *Vibrio vulnificus*, *Vibrio parahaemolyticus* |
| Later in the course | Hospital infections, melioidosis and cholera in the organ blocks |
